Stone Family KitchenThe Family StoneMeet the family. Drop the strata.Every recipe serves 4.
    To StartMainsSomething SweetTo Drink
    To StartStone family pigs in blanketsBacon wrapped sausages glazed in maple, cranberry mustard dipHow to make it20 chipolatas10 rashers of streaky bacon2 tbsp maple syrup150g cranberry sauce2 tbsp wholegrain mustardCut the bacon rashers in half and wrap each chipolata.Lay on a lined tray and roast at 200°C, turning once, until crisp.Brush with maple syrup for the last few minutes.Mix the cranberry sauce with wholegrain mustard for dipping and serve hot on toothpicks.Dinner table garlic herb pull-apartJulie trips off the bus and wins everyone over. Garlic herb butter loaf.How to make it500g crusty loaf100g butter3 garlic cloves1 bunch of parsley30g parmesanCut the loaf in deep diagonal slices every 2cm, without cutting through the base.Mash the soft butter with crushed garlic, parsley and parmesan.Push the butter into every cut and wrap in foil.Bake at 190°C.Open the foil and bake until crisp and golden.MainsHam, spinach and gruyère strataBread and egg bake with ham and gruyère. A Morton family tradition.How to make it20g butter6 thick slices of day-old bread200g leg ham100g baby spinach150g gruyère6 eggs500ml full cream milk1 tbsp Dijon mustard1 jar of tomato relishButter a 2L baking dish.Tear the bread and layer with the diced ham, spinach and grated gruyère.Whisk the eggs with milk, Dijon, salt and pepper and pour over.Press down and cover.Chill for at least 2 hours or overnight.Bake at 180°C until puffed and golden.Rest before serving with tomato relish.Sybil's lemon and thyme roast chickenRoast chicken, Christmas Eve, and one very wrong choice of wordsHow to make it1.8kg whole chicken60g butter, soft3 garlic cloves, crushed1 small bunch thyme2 lemons1kg potatoes, cut in chunks2 tbsp olive oilMix the butter with the garlic, thyme leaves, zest of a lemon and salt.Push the butter under the chicken skin and put the halved lemons and thyme stalks in the cavity.Toss the potatoes with the oil and salt in a roasting tin and sit the chicken on top.Roast at 200°C until the juices run clear.Rest for 10 minutes, then carve and spoon the pan juices over.Something SweetChristmas morning cinnamon scrollsCinnamon scrolls, handed out like the framed photosHow to make it500g pizza dough90g butter80g brown sugar2 tsp ground cinnamon120g cream cheese150g icing sugar1 tsp vanilla extractRoll the dough into a 30 x 40cm rectangle.Spread with soft butter and sprinkle with brown sugar mixed with cinnamon.Roll up from the long side and cut into scrolls.Pack into a greased 24cm tin and cover.Rest until puffy.Bake at 190°C until golden.Beat the cream cheese, butter, icing sugar and vanilla and spread over the warm scrolls.To DrinkStone house eggnog latteStrong coffee, eggnog milk, nutmeg. Meredith can make more.How to make it500ml full cream milk150ml thickened cream3 tbsp caster sugar1 cinnamon stick1 tsp vanilla extract2 eggs400ml brewed coffee1 whole nutmegHeat the milk with cream, sugar, cinnamon stick and vanilla until steaming.Whisk the egg yolks in a bowl and pour in the hot milk while whisking.Return to the pan and stir over low heat until slightly thick.Brew strong coffee and divide between mugs.Froth the eggnog milk, pour over and grate nutmeg on top.
